data.narrative: Applied the Context Triangle to the real codebase, chose a layered context strategy, verified convention matching with 15 live error probes, and found and fixed a real defect in the codebase's own error-redaction utility that was mangling 401 messages.

dimension_scores.observation: Context engineering micro-exercise sorted the ACTUAL fork files into the three triangle buckets, and the layered strategy was chosen with articulated tradeoffs.
dimension_scores.evidence: M3 CONTEXT proof: architectural (links.py, errors.py, main.py), local (models, deps, schemas), constraint (requirements, error format).

dimension_scores.observation: Ran 15 live error probes across existing and team endpoints instead of trusting static comparison; caught the redaction bug that a code-read alone could miss.
dimension_scores.evidence: compare_errors/2/401 scripts: 400/401/403/404/409 envelopes byte-identical; found 'missing [REDACTED]' over-redaction.

dimension_scores.observation: The context package was complete on first pass (no agent-output divergence), and the one real bug found was fixed in a single edit with immediate verification.
dimension_scores.evidence: errors.py pattern fix verified: 4/4 unit cases + live 401 messages + 75 tests green in one iteration.

dimension_scores.observation: Correctly distinguished a codebase defect from an agent divergence -- the agent's output matched the envelope by construction; the flaw was in the convention utility itself.
dimension_scores.evidence: Traced violation to errors.py:15, not the three team outputs; fixed the pattern with a negative lookahead.

dimension_scores.observation: Shipped a genuinely fixed error-handling path: 401 clients now see 'missing bearer token' while real tokens and passwords still redact.
dimension_scores.evidence: verify_redact_live.py: 401 'missing bearer token' + 'invalid or expired token'; check_redact.py 4/4.

dimension_scores.observation: The trace-to-missing-context analysis was recorded in the proof, but the codebase-defect finding would benefit from a standalone incident note in the workspace.
dimension_scores.evidence: proof-aie-m3-break.json + proof-aie-m3-fix.json document the full trace.

strengths: Context Triangle applied to real files, not hypotheticals; layered strategy chosen with the module's own 'averages across 40 files' and 'forgot a convention' failure modes articulated.
Empirical convention matching (15 live probes) that produced byte-identical envelopes and exposed a real redaction bug.
Fixed the codebase-level defect in errors.py and verified end-to-end (unit + live + full suite).
Audited the conventions themselves rather than just whether the agent followed them.
growth_areas: Promote the errors.py redaction finding into a standalone workspace incident note so it is visible outside proof JSON.
In later modules, extend live probe coverage to happy-path response bodies, not just error envelopes.
data.recommendation: Carry the layered context discipline into Module 4: when you review AI output, also review the conventions the output was told to match -- the convention itself may be the bug.

public_evidence.student_action: Found a codebase-level error-handling bug via live convention matching and fixed it: 401 messages were rendering as 'missing [REDACTED]'.
public_evidence.technical_detail: Changed REDACTION_PATTERNS bearer regex to 'Bearer\s+(?!token\b)[A-Za-z0-9\-._~+/]+=*' so real JWTs redact but the literal phrase 'bearer token' survives.
public_evidence.proof: check_redact.py 4/4 pass; live TestClient shows 401 {'message': 'missing bearer token'}; 75 tests exit 0.
public_evidence.reviewer_value: Shows an engineer who validates error contracts empirically and fixes the conventions themselves when they are defective.
